span: if the Act does not apply, the dismissal, termination or retrenchment of the employee cannot attract Section 58 of the Act
why: About whether a statutory appeal exists when the Act does not apply; not about notice before terminating a probationer.

span: the assertion that an order of termination was not received by the employee is not relevant to hold that the termination order was fake
why: Concerns proof/receipt of a termination order and transfer-related unfair labour practice, not whether prior notice is required for probationers.

span: Justice Dipak Misra (as he then was) rejected the contention that Rule 105 of the 1973 Rules stipulated a deemed confirmation of service
why: Reports a High Court decision on deemed confirmation of a probationer; no statement about notice and not clearly adopted as the court's holding on the proposition.

span: the decision of the employer to terminate the services of the employees could not be said to have any element of public policy
why: Reports precedents on writ maintainability against employers; different issue.

span: the employee/recruit is not to be discharged/terminated axiomatically from service just by a stroke of pen
why: Limits discharge of a recruit for suppression of facts; the passage does not say the person is a probationer or whether notice is required.

span: the employer is certainly entitled to indicate the specialisation that is expected

if the employer simply terminates the services of a probationer without holding an enquiry and without giving him a reasonable chance of showing cause against his removal from service, the probationary civil servant can have no cause of action
why: Quoted precedent (emphasis supplied, adoption not explicit) states both that simple termination needs no enquiry/show-cause and that punitive discharge without enquiry is struck down.

span: the gratuity of an employee, whose services have been terminated for any act, wilful omission or negligence
The situation of an owner of property, executing a lease agreement in respect of his property cannot be equated with a contract of employment
why: Dealership/lease agreement dispute; employment case only distinguished.

span: the employee/ 738 Digital Supreme Court Reports recruit is not to be discharged/terminated axiomatically from service just by a stroke of pen
why: Same discharge-for-suppression principle; probationary status and notice not addressed in the passage.

span: In such cases of ‘stigmatic’ removal only a reasonable opportunity of hearing is sine-qua-non.
why: Holding: probationers can be relieved if unsuitable, but stigmatic removal requires a hearing; the answer depends on whether termination is stigmatic.

span: non-compliance with Section 25F would not vitiate the orders of termination
why: Reports M Venugopal: probationer termination under regulation is not retrenchment, so no s.25F notice/compensation; passage does not show present court adopting it.

span: he could be terminated from service during the period of probation without holding any inquiry
why: Reports an earlier holding (suppression of information by a probationer); narrower condition and adoption by the present court not shown here.

span: the employer is under an obligation to comply with the twin conditions of Section 25F of the Act 1947 before the retrenchment is given effect to
why: General rule for workmen with 240 days' service; whether a probationer is covered (or excepted) is not stated.
